lines.text: A man is loading boxes into a pickup truck. He stops dead at the sight of me, like he'd memorized every face in town and mine doesn't fit.

lines.speaker: Ernesto
lines.text: You new around here? I... I don't see new faces too often.

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: My car broke down on the highway. I'm staying a night at the motel.

lines.speaker: Ernesto
lines.text: The motel. Sure. Good luck with that.
He says it like a private joke he's got no plans to explain. He goes back to loading boxes without looking at me again.

topics.displayName: Ask about his shop and last night

lines.text: The crumpled receipt is still on the counter. I bring it up in passing.

lines.speaker: Ernesto
lines.text: What about it? A bad month. Two. People don't buy good carpet anymore, they buy that synthetic junk.

lines.speaker: Ernesto
lines.text: I don't know why you're asking about my business. I had nothing to do with what happened at the motel.
Nobody mentioned the motel. He brings it up himself, unprompted.

lines.speaker: Ernesto
lines.text: The shop is what it is. Not much of a life, but it's mine.

lines.speaker: Ernesto
lines.text: Used to sell well. Now people just pass by. And with what happened at the motel, even worse.
He talks about the shop like he's talking about himself. With the same resignation.
I show him the olive-green fiber. It's the same kind he sells.

lines.speaker: Ernesto
lines.text: That proves nothing. I've sold that carpet for years, half the town has it.

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: You said you were closing up the shop that night. Your hours don't run that late.

lines.speaker: Ernesto
lines.text: What do you want me to say? I was there. Alone. Nobody saw me, but I was there.
He touches his hand without realizing it. A fresh cut, poorly bandaged, peeks out from under his sleeve.

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: And that?

lines.speaker: Ernesto
lines.text: A can. Cut myself on a can opening boxes. Now even that matters to you?
He doesn't name Robert. Not once. But he doesn't look away either, when he could.

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: You said you were closing up the shop that night.

lines.speaker: Ernesto
lines.text: Yeah. That's what happened. What else do you want me to say?
He crosses his arms. The cut on his hand barely peeks out from under his sleeve.

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: And that hand?

lines.speaker: Ernesto
lines.text: A can. Nothing. We done?
There's not much more to get out of him. I still don't have anything real to press with.
